title: Wayfair — Shopping Application Rehearsal
briefing: A candidate reports an August 2024 frontend interview, published December 30, 2025, covering product listings, ratings, cart state, persistence, and inventory updates. Design a storefront with product discovery, reviews, and a persistent cart. This exercise adapts a public candidate report; company attribution and interview details are not independently verified. The practice constraints and follow-ups are Codematica additions. Use your own timer and drawing tool: 45 minutes designing, 10 minutes handling follow-ups, and 5 minutes reviewing. No coding is required. Your design is not automatically graded; reflection text is transient. The related lesson contains the source and shared rubric.
objectives: Distinguish products from purchasable variants. Define cart lines, quantities, prices, and availability.
Draw listing → product detail → cart, showing URL state, cached server data, and unsaved interaction state.
State the cart merge policy. Explain which values the server must validate before purchase and how the UI communicates changes without silently discarding user choices.

prediction.prompt: Which area is most likely to expose a weakness in your first design?

options.label: An uncertain request outcome or recovery gap.
Performance or accessibility under the stated constraints.

steps.title: 0–7 minutes: clarify the scope
steps.instructions: Design a storefront with product discovery, reviews, and a persistent cart. Identify two main journeys, required devices, freshness, permissions, and exclusions. Separate requirements from assumptions.

steps.title: 7–20 minutes: draw the architecture
steps.instructions: Draw listing → product detail → cart, showing URL state, cached server data, and unsaved interaction state. Assign state owners and component inputs/events. Include loading, empty, and error states.

steps.title: 20–30 minutes: define data and APIs
steps.instructions: Distinguish products from purchasable variants. Define cart lines, quantities, prices, and availability. Specify one read and one write, including identities, response fields, cache policy, and safe retry conditions.

steps.title: 30–45 minutes: trace behavior and recovery
steps.instructions: Trace one interaction from input to confirmed state, then fail a request. State the cart merge policy. Explain which values the server must validate before purchase and how the UI communicates changes without silently discarding user choices.

steps.title: 45–55 minutes: handle follow-ups
steps.instructions: A guest signs in with an existing account cart. A product sells out. Prices change. Two browser tabs update the cart. Pick the hardest case and show which decisions change. State any unresolved limits.

steps.title: 55–60 minutes: review your evidence
steps.instructions: Score scope, components, state and data, APIs and consistency, failure recovery, and quality and trade-offs. Use 0: missing, 1: mentioned, 2: explained with a concrete decision and consequence. Check only evidence you can show. Choose the weakest dimension and redraw it; this is not an employer hiring threshold.

evidenceChecklist.label: I stated the main journeys, assumptions, and exclusions.
I drew component responsibilities and interaction contracts.
I assigned state owners, stable identities, and invariants.
I defined reads, writes, caching, and reconciliation.
I traced one failure through usable recovery.
I defended accessibility, performance, measurement, and alternatives.
I defined guest/account cart merging and traced a price or inventory change before purchase.

reflectionPrompts: State the cart merge policy. Explain which values the server must validate before purchase and how the UI communicates changes without silently discarding user choices.
Which decision changed after a follow-up, and what requirement caused it?
Which dimension was weakest, and what will you redraw next time?
extensionChallenge: Defend your rendering choices, then change the assumption: discovery must work on a slow mobile connection while cart updates arrive from another tab.
